events.title: Niccolò Machiavelli is born in Florence
events.description: The future diplomat and writer was born in the Republic of Florence. He went on to write The Prince, a frank and unsentimental guide to winning and keeping political power.
events.significance: Machiavelli is often called a founding figure of modern political theory, and his name is still shorthand for hard-nosed political calculation.

events.title: Columbus reaches Jamaica
events.description: On his second voyage to the Americas, Christopher Columbus arrived at Jamaica. He named the island Santiago.
events.significance: The landing began Spain's presence on Jamaica, which shaped the island's history for generations.

events.title: Poland adopts Europe's first modern written constitution
events.description: Poland and Lithuania's Commonwealth introduced a reforming constitution. It aimed to strengthen the state and modernize its government.
events.significance: The constitution lasted barely a year, but it became a lasting symbol of Polish national identity. Poland and Lithuania still mark May 3 as Constitution Day.

events.title: Japan's postwar constitution takes effect
events.description: Japan's new constitution came into force. It granted universal suffrage and reduced Emperor Hirohito to a symbolic role.
events.significance: It reshaped Japan as a parliamentary democracy and remains the country's governing document.

events.title: First aircraft lands at the North Pole
events.description: US Air Force Lieutenant Colonels Joseph O. Fletcher and William P. Benedict landed a plane at the North Pole.
events.significance: The landing was a milestone in polar aviation and Arctic exploration.
